title: IC cards & tickets
body:
Buy a Nimoca card (Nishitetsu's regional IC card) at any subway/railway ticket machine or the airport bus counter — ¥2,000 total (¥500 refundable deposit + ¥1,500 usable credit), top-up to ¥20,000. Nationwide cards (Suica, Pasmo, Icoca, Sugoca) all work interchangeably on the subway, Nishitetsu, JR Kyushu and local buses, so anyone already holding one from a prior Japan trip doesn't need a second card.

There's no group-gate — each of the 8 taps in individually at the ticket gate, same as everywhere else in Japan. Budget a few extra seconds at gates during busy periods. Nimoca refunds (minus a ¥220 fee) aren't available at the airport's International Terminal, so cash out downtown if anyone wants their deposit back before flying home.

title: Key transit routes
steps: Fukuoka Airport → Hakata/Tenjin. International arrivals: take the free shuttle bus to the Domestic Terminal first (every 5–15 min). From the Domestic Terminal, the Kuko subway line reaches Hakata in ≈5 min (≈¥260) and Tenjin in ≈11 min (≈¥260) — one of the shortest airport-to-downtown links in Japan.

Hakata/Tenjin → Dazaifu, by train. Nishitetsu Tenjin-Omuta Line from Nishitetsu Fukuoka (Tenjin) Station to Nishitetsu-Futsukaichi Station, then transfer to the Dazaifu Line for the last stop. No through train — always one transfer. ⚠ Nishitetsu raised fares system-wide Apr 1, 2026; the current fare is ≈¥480 per an unconfirmed aggregator figure (the last officially-confirmed pre-revision figure was ¥400) — confirm at the ticket machine.

Hakata/Fukuoka Airport → Dazaifu, by direct bus. The Nishitetsu Dazaifu Liner "Tabito" runs direct with no transfer: from Hakata Bus Terminal (¥800, ≈40 min) or Fukuoka Airport's International Terminal (¥700, ≈25 min), ¥20 cheaper by IC/credit card, no reservation. Frequent (28 trips/day weekdays, 36–37 weekends) but can deny boarding once full — for a party of 8, aim for an off-peak departure or be ready to split across two buses.

Hakata/Tenjin → Itoshima. JR Chikuhi Line from Meinohama reaches Chikuzen-Maebaru Station, the jumping-off point for Itoshima's coast. The train does NOT reach the coastal sights themselves (Sakurai Futamigaura, Shiraito Falls) — a Showa Bus connection or a taxi covers the last leg. Bus frequency on these coastal routes is sparse; given the group's size and the distance between sights, a taxi or rental car for the day is the realistic way to see more than one Itoshima stop.

Getting to Nokonoshima Island Park. The Fukuoka City Municipal Ferry runs from Meinohama to Nokonoshima — ¥230 one-way, 10 min, roughly hourly (≈23 sailings/day, first ≈5:00, last ≈23:00). A connecting Nishitetsu bus (≈10 min) covers the short hop from the ferry terminal to the park itself.

title: Last trains & buffers
body: Exact last-train times for the Nishitetsu Dazaifu Line and the JR Chikuhi Line aren't pinned to a specific weekday — both operators' printable timetables are image-only PDFs, and both lines had schedule revisions in March 2026. As a planning buffer: aim to leave Dazaifu or Itoshima's coast by early evening, and target arriving back at the connecting station at least 90 minutes before you'd expect a last train, rather than cutting it close to an unconfirmed time.
